Elephant Movement Metrics Calculator

Clean GPS collar data and calculate movement metrics, on your own computer.

Your tracking data never leaves this computer

Monitoring elephant movement across Africa

This tool calculates standardised movement metrics from elephant GPS tracking data. It is part of the Continental Elephant Tracking Initiative (CTI), coordinated by Save the Elephants, which uses the same metrics from tracking projects across Africa to set baselines for how elephants move and to detect when that movement changes.

Definitions and diagrams for all 23 metrics the tool calculates

1. CalculateTurn your GPS collar data into movement metrics, on your own computer.
2. ShareSend the metrics (no locations) to the CTI to include your population in the research.
3. MonitorFollow your own elephants' metrics over time and compare them with other populations.

1. Load your tracking data

A CSV or Excel export from your collar system (EarthRanger, Movebank, Africa Wildlife Tracking, Vectronic, Lotek, ...). One row per GPS fix.

Load all your files for this study area at once, covering the whole time since the collars were fitted, not just your latest download. Select or drop several files together; overlapping downloads are fine (repeated fixes are removed). If you saved the combined tracking data file from a previous run, load it together with your new download(s).

How should your data be formatted?

  • An elephant name or ID column
  • A date and time for each fix (one column, or separate date and time columns)
  • Coordinates: latitude/longitude in decimal degrees, UTM easting/northing, or a WKT "POINT (lon lat)" column
  • Optional: sex, species, collar ID, study area (you can also enter sex later)

Extra columns are fine (speed, temperature, battery, DOP, ...): they are ignored. Column names do not have to match exactly; you can check and change which column is which in the next step.

Example:

namesextimestamplatitudelongitudecollar_idtemperature
KitoF2023-03-01 00:00:000.5681237.53104STE-441221.5
KitoF2023-03-01 01:00:000.5693037.53288STE-441220.9
KitoF2023-03-01 02:00:000.5710237.53511STE-441220.1
BarakaM2023-03-01 00:00:000.6147737.48820STE-452022.3
BarakaM2023-03-01 01:00:000.6165937.49013STE-452021.8

Any extra columns, such as those shaded above, are fine to leave in.

Fixes should be about 1-4 hours apart. Collars with a typical interval longer than 6 hours cannot be used for these metrics and are skipped.

Already used this tool to calculate metrics? Drop the *_metrics.csv file it made here to look at your results again and compare them with other populations.

2. Check the columns we found

We guessed which column holds what. Please check, and change any that are wrong.

Coordinates: latitude and longitude in decimal degrees are all that is needed. UTM easting/northing or a WKT column are only used when a file has no latitude/longitude.

Used to decide day and night (06:00-18:00 local).

First rows of your file

3. Study area and elephants

If some elephants belong to a different study area, add it here, then choose it for those elephants in the Study area column of the table below.

Elephants found

Sex is needed for the male/female comparisons. Set any that are missing or wrong.

There is one row for each collar an elephant wore. Rows with the same elephant name are treated as one elephant. If several collar IDs belong to one elephant, give their rows the same name. If two different elephants share a name, change the name in one of their rows.

4. Calculating

Cleaning the tracks automatically, resampling to 4-hour steps and computing 23 metrics. Large datasets can take a few minutes; keep this tab open.
